ui.title: World Solutions Map
ui.desc: An interactive world map of every Saving Planets solution: green pins are working now, blue pins are coming soon, and rocket pins show upcoming launches.
ui.lead: Tap a pin to see a solution, where it works and a link to its page. Green pins are active now, blue pins are coming soon, and rocket pins list the next launches from that site.
ui.orbitintro: These solutions work in space, so they have no single place on Earth. Pins mark a launch site only when the solution page names it.
ui.worldintro: These solutions happen all over the planet, with no single place to pin.
ui.listintro: The same information as the map, for screen readers and keyboards.
ui.src: Launch data: The Space Devs Launch Library 2 (same feed as our Live Launch Tracker). Launches by Russia, China and North Korea are not shown.
ui.pins: {t} solutions: {g} active · {b} coming soon · {r} launch sites
ui.label: Interactive world map of solutions and launch sites
ui.listmore: Every solution as a list, including the ones in orbit and worldwide

sols.s: 4ocean removes plastic from oceans, rivers, and coastlines with full-time cleanup crews, funded by products made from recovered plastic.
The Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi tracks more than 18.5 million mangroves planted across over 1,775 hectares with its new Mangrove Observatory.

p.label: Abu Dhabi coast, United Arab Emirates

sols.s: Aditya-L1 is ISRO's first space-based solar observatory, studying the Sun from a halo orbit around L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth.
Each year, Adopt-a-Beach volunteers remove tens of thousands of pounds of litter from Great Lakes beaches, about 85% of it plastic.
ESA guided its retired Aeolus wind satellite down in the first assisted reentry of its kind, cutting the already low debris risk by a factor of 150.
African Parks manages 24 protected areas in 13 countries, covering over 20 million hectares, in partnership with governments and local communities (nonprofit).
More than 20 kelp farms grow ribbon, giant, bull and sugar kelp in Alaska's cold, nutrient-rich waters (Alaska Mariculture Alliance).

p.label: Kodiak, Alaska (Alaska Sea Grant mariculture specialists)
Kasaan Bay, Southeast Alaska (new kelp farm leases)

sols.n: Alaska SeaLife Center: Marine Wildlife Rescue
sols.s: The Alaska SeaLife Center in Seward is a nonprofit aquarium and research center that rescues stranded marine animals…
JAXA's DAICHI-4 radar sees through clouds over a 200 km swath, continuing the radar record used for deforestation alerts.
Since 1875, American Forests has worked to restore U.S. forests, from big natural landscapes to city streets, with more than 63 million trees planted.
American Rivers has worked directly on more than 200 dam removals; in 2025 the U.S. removed 100 dams and reconnected more than 4,893 river miles.
Since 1972, the Arbor Day Foundation says it has planted more than half a billion trees, working in more than 60 countries (nonprofit figures).
Close to 4,000 robotic floats dive through the ocean and send back temperature and salinity data, free to everyone. The 3 millionth profile came in 2024.

p.label: Argo Program Office, Scripps Institution of Oceanography, San Diego

sols.s: A satellite system that tracks wildlife and ocean instruments from tiny transmitters, following more than 8,000 animals every month for conservation science.

p.label: NOAA Office of Satellite and Product Operations, Suitland, Maryland

sols.s: ESA's Ariel will study the atmospheres of a thousand planets orbiting other stars, revealing what they are made of (ESA).

p.label: Europe's Spaceport, Kourou, French Guiana (planned launch site)

sols.s: NASA's Artemis program: Artemis I flew in 2022, Artemis II carried four astronauts 252,756 miles from Earth in April 2026, and Artemis III is targeted for 2027.
Astroscale inspects, services and removes debris in orbit: ELSA-d, ADRAS-J's 2024 close-up of an H-IIA upper stage, and ADRAS-J2, targeted for fiscal 2027.

sols.n: ATLAS Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System
sols.s: Four robotic telescopes, two in Hawaiʻi, search the entire dark sky every 24 hours for asteroids that could hit Earth, so people can be warned.

p.label: ATLAS telescope, Mauna Loa, Hawaiʻi Island
ATLAS telescope, El Sauce Observatory, Chile

sols.s: Atmospheric drag is Earth's natural space debris removal: it pulls low-orbit junk down to burn up, faster when the Sun is active, but barely works up high.
In Oregon's Bridge Creek, beavers given simple dam starters raised juvenile steelhead survival 52% and production 175% (NOAA Fisheries).
After eight years in space, BepiColombo enters orbit around Mercury on 21 November 2026, the first mission to put two spacecraft there (ESA).
A New York nonprofit restoring the harbor with oyster reefs, aiming for one billion oysters by 2030 (nonprofit figures).
ESA's Biomass satellite, launched April 29, 2025, carries the first P-band radar in space, seeing through forest canopies to measure the carbon stored in trees.
In January 2023, the U.S. EPA used Clean Water Act section 404(c) to limit mine waste disposal in Bristol Bay headwaters near the Pebble deposit.

p.label: Pebble deposit area, Bristol Bay watershed, Alaska

sols.s: Carbfix dissolves carbon dioxide in water and injects it into basalt rock, where it turns into stone (company).
The first mission dedicated to Earth's exosphere, Carruthers watches our planet's ultraviolet halo from about a million miles sunward.
A NASA-funded survey in Arizona that has discovered more near-Earth objects than any other: 17,918 near-Earth asteroids since 1995.

p.label: Lunar and Planetary Laboratory, University of Arizona, Tucson

sols.s: Seoul removed an ageing road and elevated motorway that covered the Cheonggyecheon stream and restored it along a 5.84 km corridor through the city centre.
Since 1966, the Chesapeake Bay Foundation has worked to save the Bay and its rivers, adding more than 21 million oysters in fiscal year 2026 (CBF).
CHIME will image Earth in more than 200 colours of light to support sustainable farming, food security and biodiversity (ESA).
Two Copernicus satellites will measure sea ice, sea-surface temperature and salinity over 95% of the globe every day, with sub-daily polar views (ESA).
Clean Lakes Alliance works to improve water quality in Madison's Yahara lakes; it reports 81 monitoring stations and over $1.4 million in grants (its figures).
Clean Up the Lake removes submerged litter from freshwater lakes using scuba divers and volunteers, and GPS-pins, sorts and weighs every piece it finds.
ClearSpace leads Europe's first active debris removal mission and provides in-orbit servicing. It is a privately held in-orbit servicing company.
Three spacecraft will wait in space for a fresh comet and fly past it together to make a 3D map; launch is planned for late 2028 or early 2029 (ESA).
Europe's air monitoring service forecasts air pollution, smoke and dust worldwide twice a day for more than 23,500 users, free and open.

sols.n: Copernicus CO2M Carbon Dioxide Monitoring (ESA / EU)
sols.s: A planned trio of satellites that will measure the carbon dioxide and methane people release, so countries can check whether their emission cuts are working.

sols.n: Copernicus Emergency Management Service: On-Demand Mapping
sols.s: The European Union's emergency mapping service turns satellite images into maps for disaster teams, 24/7 since 2012, with more than 1,000 activations.
Free, open ocean data and forecasts for the whole planet. In 2025 users downloaded almost 15,000 terabytes of ocean data from Copernicus Marine.
Sentinel-1 radar sees through clouds, day and night, to map floods, earthquakes and ice; Sentinel-1C and 1D joined in 2024 and 2025.
Sentinel-2C joined the Copernicus fleet in September 2024, imaging land and coasts in 13 bands so forests and crops are checked every five days.
The Copernicus Sentinel-3 satellites measure Earth's oceans, land, ice and atmosphere, and a third satellite, Sentinel-3C, launched on September 15, 2026 (ESA).

p.label: Sentinel-3C launched from Europe's Spaceport, French Guiana

sols.s: From geostationary orbit on MTG-S1, Sentinel-4 measures air pollution such as nitrogen dioxide and ozone over Europe and North Africa every hour (ESA).

p.label: EUMETSAT, Darmstadt, Germany (operates MTG-S1, which carries Sentinel-4)

sols.s: Copernicus Sentinel-5P maps the gases in the air we breathe, covering the whole planet every day with its Tropomi instrument (ESA).
Sentinel-6B, launched November 17, 2025, continues the precise record of global sea level that began in the early 1990s.
Coral Gardeners grows corals in nurseries and replants them on reefs in French Polynesia, Fiji and Thailand: 238,250 corals planted so far.
Researchers capture coral spawn and rear millions of baby corals for damaged reefs; the first Coral IVF corals reproduced on the Great Barrier Reef in 2021.
NOAA's Coral Reef Watch uses satellites to warn of the ocean heat that bleaches corals, with daily monitoring of 95% of the world's coral reefs.

p.label: NOAA Center for Weather and Climate Prediction, College Park, Maryland

sols.s: Coral Restoration Foundation had returned 253,833 corals to Florida's reefs by the end of 2024 (organization figure). Florida's Coral Reef in the Florida Keys.
Coral Vita grows reef-building corals on land up to 50 times faster than in nature, and says it has grown over 100,000 corals (company figures).

p.label: Grand Bahama, The Bahamas (Coral Vita coral farm)

sols.n: Costa Rica Payments for Environmental Services (FONAFIFO)
sols.s: Costa Rica's FONAFIFO pays the owners of forests and forest plantations for the environmental services they provide, under Forestry Law 7575 (FONAFIFO).

sols.n: CRISTAL Polar Ice and Snow Altimeter (ESA)
sols.s: CRISTAL will carry the first dual-frequency radar altimeter to measure polar sea-ice thickness and the snow on top, following ESA's CryoSat (ESA).

p.label: Airbus, Friedrichshafen, Germany, where CRISTAL-A is being assembled

sols.s: CryoSat measures polar sea ice and the great ice sheets from space, and its data revealed 85 hidden lakes under Antarctica (ESA).
Digital Earth Africa turns satellite data into free and open maps of water, farmland and coasts for the whole African continent (Digital Earth Africa).

p.label: icipe, Nairobi, Kenya (host of the programme)

sols.s: NASA's Dragonfly is a car-size rotorcraft that will fly across Saturn's moon Titan to study the chemistry that came before life (NASA).

p.label: Launching from Kennedy Space Center, Florida

sols.s: NASA's EPIC camera rides on NOAA's DSCOVR spacecraft at the L1 point, photographing the entire sunlit face of Earth several times a day, with an archive...

p.label: NOAA Satellite Operations Facility, Suitland, Maryland (mission control)

sols.s: ESA–JAXA EarthCARE carries the first space cloud radar that can measure how cloud particles move up and down, sharpening forecasts of how clouds affect climate.
Eden: People+Planet restores landscapes with local communities, including a 394,000-hectare project in Tanzania's Rubeho Mountains (Eden).
Two Elwha River dams came down between 2011 and 2014, and more than 20 million tons of trapped sediment flowed downstream to rebuild the river and coast.
The UAE's Hope Probe has studied the Martian atmosphere from orbit since 2021, and its mission is now extended until 2028 (UAE Space Agency).

p.label: UAE Space Agency, United Arab Emirates

sols.s: NASA's EMIT instrument on the International Space Station maps the minerals in desert dust and has spotted methane super-emitters from space (NASA JPL).
Saturn’s small moon Enceladus hides a global ocean and sprays it into space. Cassini found water, salts, organics, hydrogen and phosphates there.
ESA's EnVision will study Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, and may show how a planet like ours got so hot. Launch is planned for late 2031.
India's EOS-06, the third Oceansat, tracks ocean color, sea-surface temperature and winds; it imaged Cyclone Mandous and an algal bloom on day one.
NASA's twin ESCAPADE spacecraft will study how the solar wind strips Mars' atmosphere, after an Earth slingshot in fall 2026.

p.label: UC Berkeley Space Sciences Laboratory (mission lead and operations)

sols.s: NASA's Europa Clipper is on its way to Jupiter's ocean moon, with an Earth gravity assist on December 3, 2026 and 49 close Europa flybys from 2030.
Europe's wildfire system forecasts fire danger and maps burnt areas from satellites. In 2024 it mapped wildfires in 42 countries.

p.label: European Commission Joint Research Centre, Ispra, Italy

sols.s: Europe's first Mars rover, Rosalind Franklin, will drill 2 meters down to look for signs of past life, targeting launch in 2028.
Earth Fire Alliance's FireSat satellites are built to spot wildfires as small as 5 by 5 meters from space and get the data to firefighters fast.

sols.n: FIRMS Fire Information for Resource Management System (NASA)
sols.s: NASA's FIRMS delivers satellite fire detections within 3 hours anywhere on Earth, and in real time for the US and Canada. Free for firefighters and everyone.
Launched together on September 15, 2026, ESA's FLEX maps the faint glow of photosynthesis while Sentinel-3C watches oceans and land.

p.label: Launched from Europe's Spaceport, French Guiana

sols.s: By thinning small trees, forest elephants help central Africa's rainforests store more carbon: 26 to 60 more tonnes of biomass per hectare (Nature Geoscience).

p.label: Brazzaville, Republic of Congo (WCS Congo, forest elephant program)

sols.s: ESA's FORUM will measure Earth's outgoing far-infrared radiation, never measured from space before, filling a missing piece of the climate jigsaw (ESA).

p.label: Europe's Spaceport, Kourou, French Guiana (planned launch site)

sols.s: FreshWater Watch trains citizen scientists to test rivers, lakes and ponds: 80,000+ datasets from 22,000+ volunteers (organization figures).
Gaganyaan G1, ISRO's first uncrewed Gaganyaan flight, is targeted for late 2026 on the human-rated HLVM3 rocket (ISRO).

p.label: Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, India (launch site)

sols.s: Europe's Galileo is the world's most precise satellite navigation system, serving over five billion smartphone users and helping rescues (ESA).
Galápagos Conservancy and the Galápagos National Park Directorate rear giant tortoises in breeding centres and return them to their home islands.
Japan's SHIKISAI satellite checks the health of Earth from space every 2 or 3 days, tracking clouds, aerosols, ocean color, plants, snow and ice (JAXA).
GEDI fires lasers from the International Space Station to measure the height and 3D shape of Earth's forests (University of Maryland).

p.label: University of Maryland, College Park (mission lead)

sols.s: NOAA's next generation of geostationary weather satellites, planned from 2032, will improve warnings of severe weather and hazards (NOAA).
Global Fishing Watch uses satellites and SI to map fishing; its 2024 Nature study found about 75% of industrial fishing vessels are not publicly tracked.
Free global river flood forecasts up to 30 days ahead, plus 4-month outlooks, from the Copernicus Emergency Management Service.
Free satellite forest data and deforestation alerts from WRI; where Indigenous forest monitors used it, deforestation fell 52% in one year.
Globe at Night invites anyone to measure how dark their night sky is. People have sent 331,065 observations to track light pollution (program figures).
NOAA's GOES-19 carries CCOR-1, the world's first operational space-based coronagraph, imaging the Sun's corona every 15 minutes.

p.label: NOAA Satellite Operations Facility, Suitland, Maryland (mission control)

sols.s: JAXA's IBUKI GW tracks carbon dioxide, methane and nitrogen dioxide while also measuring the water cycle. Launched June 29, 2025 from Tanegashima Space Center.
Twin US-German satellites weigh Earth's water by measuring gravity, tracking groundwater, ice and sea level since 2018. Active.
An African-led effort to restore land across the Sahel. A 2020 UN status report counted about 4 million hectares restored inside the Great Green Wall zone.
The Great Lakes Plastic Cleanup captures plastic across the world's largest freshwater system using Seabins, drones, and beach robots.
JAXA's Global Satellite Mapping of Precipitation maps rain around the world every hour, used by 18,673 registered users in 163 countries and regions.

sols.n: Gulf of Alaska Keeper: Marine Debris Cleanup
sols.s: Gulf of Alaska Keeper (GoAK) is a nonprofit that removes marine debris from the remote shores of Prince William Sound and the northern Gulf of Alaska (GoAK).

p.label: Montague Island, Prince William Sound, Alaska

sols.s: On 5 July 2026, JAXA's Hayabusa2 passed about 400 m above asteroid Torifune, the closest flyby of any Solar System body so far (JAXA).
Since 1985, Heal the Bay has worked to make the coastal waters and watersheds of Greater Los Angeles safe, healthy and clean (Heal the Bay).
Volunteer divers recover ghost nets: Healthy Seas reports 1,309.1 tons of nets and marine litter removed since 2013 (Healthy Seas figure).
ESA's Hera arrives at the asteroid Dimorphos in November 2026 to measure what NASA's DART impact did, turning deflection into a repeatable defense.
ESA's first Scout mission uses reflected navigation-satellite signals to measure soil moisture, wetlands and frozen ground (ESA).
NASA's ICESat-2 laser fires 10,000 pulses a second to measure ice sheets, sea ice, forests and coastal seafloor in 3D. Active.
NASA's IMAP watches the Sun from about a million miles sunward and can give about a half hour's warning of incoming radiation.

p.label: Johns Hopkins APL, Laurel, Maryland (mission operations)

sols.s: India's INSAT-3DS watches weather, land and oceans from geostationary orbit and carries a search-and-rescue transponder (ISRO).

p.label: Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, India (launch site)

sols.n: International Charter: Space and Major Disasters
sols.s: When disaster strikes, 17 space agencies and satellite operators pool their satellites and give free images to rescue teams. Activated 1,000 times.
Since 1986, more than 19 million volunteers have collected more than 400 million pounds of trash from beaches and waterways (Ocean Conservancy).

p.label: Texas coast, where the first Cleanup was held in 1986

sols.s: About 100 scientists from the UK, US, South Korea, Germany and Sweden are working out how fast Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier could raise sea levels (ITGC).
The space station now recycles 98% of the water its crews bring along, thanks to a Brine Processor Assembly, technology that matters wherever water is scarce.

p.label: NASA Johnson Space Center, Houston (ISS mission control)

sols.s: NOAA's polar weather satellites circle Earth 14 times a day. Polar-orbiting satellites supply about 85% of the data used by weather prediction models.
ESA's Juice will study Ganymede, Callisto and Europa, with 35 moon flybys after it reaches Jupiter in July 2031. Cruising.
Jupiter is a natural space debris removal system that swallows or flings away far more dangerous objects than any human mission could.
With farmers and pastoralists in Africa, Justdiggit is restoring 525,000 hectares of dry land and has brought back 32.3 million trees (organization figures).

sols.n: Keep Tahoe Blue (League to Save Lake Tahoe)
sols.s: Keep Tahoe Blue, the League to Save Lake Tahoe, has protected the lake for decades, and its volunteers picked up 1,330 pounds of litter after July 4, 2026.
Kelp can grow up to 18 inches a day, building underwater forests that feed and shelter thousands of species. Nature, studied and protected by NOAA and partners.
Once straightened into a canal, Florida's Kissimmee River is winding again: 44 miles of river and 20,000 acres of wetlands restored (SFWMD).
Four Klamath River dams came out by October 2024, reopening more than 400 miles of habitat to salmon, steelhead and lamprey (Klamath River Renewal).

sols.n: Lake Erie Harmful Algal Bloom Forecast (NOAA)
sols.s: NOAA forecasts and tracks toxic algae in western Lake Erie through the summer so cities and swimmers can keep drinking water and people safe (NOAA NCCOS).
Saving Planets' own lake solution: recover plastic from freshwater lakes by skimming, shoreline collection and divers, before it travels downstream to the sea.
Landsat 9 continues a 50-year record of Earth’s land, collecting 740 scenes a day and, with Landsat 8, seeing each place every 8 days.

p.label: USGS EROS Center, Sioux Falls, South Dakota (operator and data archive)

sols.s: LeoLabs runs a global network of ground radars that track satellites and debris in low Earth orbit and turn the data into collision warnings.
Libera will measure how much energy leaves Earth each day, keeping a climate record that began in 2000 going strong (NOAA).
Life Terra and its partners have planted more than 36 million trees across Europe (company figure), working toward a goal of 500 million trees.
LignoSat, the world's first wooden satellite, proved wood can survive in orbit; a follow-on is a potential solution on the horizon.
Since 1998, the Global Nature Fund's Living Lakes Network has protected and restored lakes and wetlands with 130 member organizations in more than 60 countries.
A barge-based river cleanup crew that, with more than 141,000 volunteers, has pulled over 14 million pounds of trash from U.S. rivers.
London's new super sewer catches sewage that used to spill into the River Thames in storms, with room for 1.6 million cubic metres (Tideway).

p.label: Abbey Mills Pumping Station, East London

sols.s: NASA's Lucy is touring asteroids; after Dinkinesh and Donaldjohanson, it reaches its first Trojan asteroid, Eurybates, on 11 August 2027 (NASA).
MAAP, the Monitoring of the Andes Amazon Program, is an initiative of the nonprofit Amazon Conservation that uses satellite images to report on urgent…
About 80 species of mangrove trees guard tropical coastlines: their tangled roots hold mud in place, soften storm surges and give fish food and shelter.
The MAR Insurance Programme, run by the nonprofit MAR Fund, uses parametric insurance to pay for fast reef repair after hurricanes along the 1,000 km Mesoamerican Reef.
Three weather satellites now watch Europe and Africa from 36,000 km up, with new images every 2.5 minutes and a camera that catches lightning day and night.

p.label: MTG-I2 launched from Europe's Spaceport, French Guiana

sols.s: The UN's satellite methane alert system has sent more than 3,500 alerts about major leaks in 33 countries, and responses rose from 1% to 12% in a year.
Launched August 2025 on Ariane 6, MetOp-SG-A1 carries Sentinel-5, which delivers daily global data on air pollutants, ozone and climate gases.
Founded by ocean scientist Dr. Sylvia Earle, Mission Blue backs a community-led network of 168 Hope Spots, ocean places local champions work to protect.
JAXA's MMX launches October 2026 to land on Mars's moon Phobos and return at least 10 grams of it to Earth in 2031, a first for the Mars system.
Mote scientists have restored more than 216,000 corals to Florida's Coral Reef, and their restored corals now spawn (Mote figure).
Baltimore's Trash Wheels intercept about 500 tons of trash a year before it reaches the harbor and the Chesapeake Bay (organization figure).
India's Namami Gange programme has created or rehabilitated 4,263 million litres a day of sewage treatment for the River Ganga (government figures).

p.label: Varanasi, on the River Ganga, India

sols.s: NASA's Roman telescope launched Aug 30, 2026 to L2: Hubble-sharp images 100x wider, a census of planetary systems, first images by early 2027.
Europe's asteroid watch centre computes orbits and impact risks every day and keeps a public list of every asteroid with a non-zero chance of hitting Earth.
NASA NEO Surveyor is the first space telescope built to find hazardous asteroids, including dark ones hidden in the Sun's glare. Launch NET September 2027.
NEWater is high-grade reclaimed water from PUB, Singapore's National Water Agency, made from treated used water in a three-step purification process at 4 plants.
NISAR, a NASA and ISRO radar satellite launched from India on July 30, 2025, scans nearly all of Earth's land and ice twice every 12 days, even through clouds.
Life extension in GEO: two MEVs have docked with three satellites, and the Mission Robotic Vehicle and three pods launched July 21, 2026 (company figures).
A sailing nonprofit that has pulled more than 850,000 pounds of plastic from the Pacific Gyre in 10 voyages (nonprofit figure).
NASA's OCO-2 satellite has measured carbon dioxide around the planet since 2014, showing where carbon is released and where forests and oceans absorb it.
Since 2014, One Tree Planted has planted more than 171 million trees with 489 partners in 84 countries (organization figure).
Free satellite data on how much water crops and land use, now for all 48 contiguous states, with more than 13,000 registered users.
Data centers in orbit run SI chips on solar power and radiate waste heat into space, with no water-cooling towers. Early flights only, not yet a replacement.
On April 13, 2029, asteroid Apophis passes about 20,000 miles from Earth. NASA's OSIRIS-APEX meets it in June 2029 to see how that close pass changes it.
NASA's PACE reads the color of the ocean to track phytoplankton, the base of the marine food web, plus aerosols and clouds.
The Palau National Marine Sanctuary makes about 80% of Palau's exclusive economic zone a no-take area, with the other 20% kept as a Domestic Fishing Zone.
Two telescopes on Haleakalā, Maui, that in 2021 found nearly as many near-Earth objects as the rest of the world's observatories combined.
Designated in 2025 as America's 18th national marine sanctuary, Papahānaumokuākea covers 582,570 square miles of Pacific Ocean around Hawaiʻi (NOAA).
The first spacecraft to fly through the Sun's outer atmosphere, helping scientists understand the space weather that affects life and technology on Earth.

p.label: Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, Laurel, Maryland (mission partner)

sols.s: After two dams came out of Maine's Penobscot River, nearly 5.93 million river herring climbed the Milford fish lift in 2025, up from about 590,000 in 2015.

p.label: Milford Dam fish lift, Penobscot River, Maine

sols.s: Tiny ocean plants produce about half of Earth's oxygen, making phytoplankton one of the planet's most important natural systems.
Started by a 9-year-old in 2007, Plant-for-the-Planet trains young Climate Justice Ambassadors and restores forests, including Mexico's Mayan forests.
Plastic Bank pays collectors in vulnerable communities to gather ocean-bound plastic, exchanged at local branches for income, food vouchers and school supplies.
Plastic Odyssey sets up small recycling factories in places with no recycling system, turning plastic waste into useful products and local jobs.
ESA's Plato will use 26 cameras to hunt for Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars, with launch planned for March 2027 on Ariane 6.
The Mediterranean seagrass Posidonia oceanica forms meadows that are thousands of years old and store carbon in the seafloor (CEAB-CSIC).
Predator Free 2050 is a nationwide goal to eradicate rats, possums, feral cats and mustelids from all of Aotearoa New Zealand by 2050…
Two shoebox-size NASA satellites measure the far-infrared heat that Earth's poles send into space (NASA JPL). Last reviewed: October 2026 · 4 sources cited

p.label: Launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1, New Zealand

sols.s: PRELUDE is a ClearSpace and ESA mission planned for June 2027 to validate close-proximity rendezvous technology. A potential solution on the horizon.
Project Seagrass, a UK charity, has planted more than 150,000 seagrass seeds to bring back underwater meadows (organization figures).
NASA's Psyche used a Mars flyby on 15 May 2026 to head for a metal-rich asteroid it will orbit from August 2029, to learn what a planet's core is like.
Four suitcase-sized NASA satellites image the Sun's corona and solar wind together, in 3D, since March 2025. Active in low Earth orbit.

p.label: Southwest Research Institute, Boulder, Colorado (mission lead)

sols.s: Three Canadian radar satellites watch Canada's land, coasts and Arctic day and night, through cloud and smoke, with about 250,000 images a year.

p.label: CSA Satellite Operations Control Centre, Longueuil, Quebec

sols.s: Solar-powered Guardian listening devices and SI detect chainsaws in real time; Rainforest Connection reports more than 726,000 hectares of rainforest protected.
ESA and JAXA's Ramses must launch by spring 2028 to meet Apophis before its 2029 Earth pass. Its €81.2 million build contract was signed in February 2026.
A Nevada nonprofit whose ROVs and volunteer divers pull submerged trash from Lake Tahoe, from the surface down to 1,640 feet: over 13 tons in summer 2024 alone.
Rewilding Europe helps wild nature come back across Europe. Rewilding Europe, working with local partners in large pioneering landscapes.
River Cleanup and its volunteers have recovered more than 4.39 million kg of waste from rivers worldwide and aim for 1,000 plastic-free rivers by 2050.
Every year about 27.7 million tons of Saharan dust falls on the Amazon, delivering some 22,000 tons of phosphorus that the rainforest needs (NASA).
Salt marshes are nurseries for more than 75% of fisheries species and buffer shorelines from erosion and floods (NOAA). Twice a day with the tides, all year.
NOAA's SARSAT satellites relay distress beacon signals to rescuers; the international system has supported more than 50,000 rescues worldwide since 1982 (NOAA).

p.label: U.S. SARSAT Mission Control Center, Suitland, Maryland (NOAA)

sols.s: Sea Turtle Conservancy works in 8 countries, has tagged and monitored more than 550 turtles and trained over 1,200 researchers (nonprofit figures).
Seabin's floating bins have captured 33.0 million items in Sydney Harbour since 2020, including 18.9 million microplastics (company figures).
Seagrass covers just 0.1% of the seafloor but stores 11% of the ocean's buried organic carbon, and one acre can support almost 40,000 fish, NOAA says.
SeaTrees connects people with local partners restoring mangroves, coral reefs, kelp forests and seagrass meadows around the world (SeaTrees).
SMAP maps the water in Earth's soil from space, helping improve predictions of weather, floods and droughts (NASA).

p.label: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Pasadena, California

sols.n: SOHO Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (ESA / NASA)
sols.s: Watching the Sun nonstop since 1995, SOHO helps experts predict solar storms and has found more than 5,000 comets (NASA).

p.label: Toulouse, France, where SOHO was assembled

sols.s: ESA and NASA's Solar Orbiter took the first close-up images of the Sun's poles, coming within 42 million km of the Sun. Active, orbiting the Sun.
NOAA's SOLAR-1 (formerly SWFO-L1) watches the Sun from L1, about one million miles from Earth, streaming space weather data to forecasters in real time.

p.label: NOAA headquarters, Silver Spring, Maryland (operating agency)

sols.s: Launched 11 March 2025, NASA's SPHEREx maps the whole sky in 102 infrared colors and finished its first all-sky map in 2025 (NASA JPL).
The first Otter launched October 1, 2026 for NASA's SSPICY mission, inspecting up to four dead satellites and rocket bodies from 2027.
Sungai Watch stops plastic in Indonesian rivers with trash barriers, daily collection and sorting, plus upcycling, working in Bali and Java since 2020.
Surfrider Foundation volunteers protect the ocean, waves and beaches, and in 2025 they removed 338,383 pounds of trash from U.S. coasts (Surfrider).
The Svalbard Global Seed Vault stores backup copies of the world's crop seeds free of charge, more than 100 metres inside an Arctic mountain (Seed Vault).

p.label: Svalbard Global Seed Vault, near Longyearbyen, Svalbard, Norway

sols.s: SWOT measures more than 95% of Earth's lakes larger than 15 acres and rivers wider than 330 feet, the first global survey of fresh water.
Tanager-1, built by Planet with a NASA JPL-designed spectrometer for the nonprofit Carbon Mapper, pinpoints methane and CO2 plumes from single sources.
From geostationary orbit, NASA's TEMPO measures air pollution over North America every daylight hour, a first from space (NASA).

p.label: Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory, Cambridge, Massachusetts (mission lead)

sols.s: Terraformation grows native, biodiverse forests from seed to canopy across the tropics and Hawaii, funding seed collection, nurseries, planting and monitoring.

sols.n: The Amazon Makes Its Own Rainy Season
sols.s: Water breathed out by Amazon trees starts the rainy season two to three months before winds alone would bring it (NASA JPL).
A worldwide science program where students and citizen scientists collect real environmental data: more than 293 million measurements from 127 countries.
The Great Bubble Barrier's bubble curtain guides plastic out of Amsterdam's canals into a catchment across the full width and depth, while boats and fish pass.
Saving moons, saving planets: the Moon keeps Earth's 23.5-degree tilt in check, which keeps our seasons and climate stable (NASA).
The Ocean Cleanup removes legacy plastic from ocean garbage patches and intercepts it in rivers: more than 65 million kilograms caught as of October 2026.
Deep-ocean buoys, satellites, GPS signals and seafloor cables spot tsunamis in the open ocean so coastal communities get time to reach high ground (NOAA, NASA).

p.label: Pacific Tsunami Warning Center, Ford Island, Hawaii (NOAA)
National Tsunami Warning Center, Palmer, Alaska (NOAA)

sols.s: Mobula cleanup boats catch plastic close to where it starts, and in Malaysia one boat turned 135,000 pieces of debris into community walkways (The SeaCleaners).
Three natural shields protect Earth: the heliosphere, the magnetosphere, and the atmosphere with its ozone layer, deflecting solar wind and most harmful UV-B.

sols.n: Three Trees for Every One Removed
sols.s: Saving Planets' own forest rule: plant three trees for every one removed, so each removal becomes a net gain for habitat, soil and shade, and is easy to verify.
Titan is a prebiotic time capsule, and NASA's Dragonfly rotorcraft explores it from 2034, building radar, power and autonomy tools that matter for Earth.

p.label: Dragonfly launches from Kennedy Space Center

sols.s: NASA's twin TRACERS satellites fly through Earth's polar cusps to study magnetic reconnection, a key driver of space weather.

p.label: University of Iowa, Iowa City (mission lead)

sols.s: Partnering with East African farmers on regenerative farms: 450M+ trees grown and 99,000 acres restored (nonprofit figures).
Trout Unlimited restores and reconnects cold, clean rivers, reconnecting 1,052 miles of streams in its 2024-25 season (Trout Unlimited).
NASA selected SpaceX to build the U.S. Deorbit Vehicle that will guide the International Space Station safely out of orbit after 2030.

p.label: NASA Johnson Space Center, Houston (ISS program)

sols.s: NASA's Veggie garden grows fresh food on the International Space Station; in 2015 astronauts ate the first lettuce grown in it (NASA).

p.label: NASA Johnson Space Center, Houston (ISS mission control)

sols.s: ESA's Vigil will watch the Sun from L5, giving up to four to five days' notice of certain space weather effects. Launch is planned for 2031.
Launched in 1977, the twin Voyagers are in interstellar space, and on Nov. 18, 2026, Voyager 1 will be one light-day from Earth (NASA).

p.label: Cape Canaveral, Florida, where both Voyagers launched in 1977

sols.s: Waterkeeper Alliance unites hundreds of local Waterkeeper groups that patrol and protect more than 6 million square miles of rivers, lakes and coastlines.
How the James Webb Space Telescope tracked asteroid 2024 YR4 in February 2026 and ruled out a 2032 Moon impact, two years before ground telescopes could.

p.label: Space Telescope Science Institute, Baltimore (Webb mission operations)

sols.s: WeForest has grown more than 118 million trees and has 100,000 hectares of forest under restoration and conservation (WeForest).
Whale waste carries nutrients to the ocean surface and fertilizes phytoplankton, the tiny plants at the base of the ocean food web (NOAA Fisheries).
Gray wolves returned to Yellowstone in 1995 after nearly 70 years; in January 2026 at least 84 lived in the park, in eight packs (NPS).
The Zero Debris Charter sets shared targets to stop creating space debris by 2030; by May 2026 it had 228 signatories from 34 countries (ESA).
